notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP) worked: robots.txt and plain curl/requests/curl_cffi desktop TLS profiles (chrome120/124/131, safari15_5/17_0/18_0, firefox133, edge101) were all Akamai-403'd, but curl_cffi impersonating iOS Safari (safari18_0_ios / safari184_ios) passed cleanly and returned the full 1.46MB rendered SSR page for https://www2.hm.com/en_in/home.html (200 OK) plus embedded product-carousel JSON, so no proxy/reader (r.jina.ai, translate.goog, Wayback) was used and Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome were not needed. Extracted and fully enumerated the Home department's own mega-menu taxonomy from the rendered HTML: New In, Kids: Soft toys & more (global-node-1), Monsoon Essentials (global-node-2, a weather season not a holiday - out of scope), Shop by Room (Living Room, Bedroom, Bathroom, Kitchen, Kids Room, Nursery, Outdoor), Shop by Product (Textiles, Bath & Shower, Cooking & Dining, Bed Linen, Decorations, Kids & Baby, Storage, Home Fragrance, Premium, Sleepwear - each with its full subcategory list), Sale (mirrors the same room/product split), and one generic 'seasonal-trending/trends.608.html' teaser whose on-page label is 'Minimalist dining' (a styling trend, not a holiday) - so it was excluded as non-holiday editorial content. No Christmas, Diwali, Halloween, Valentine's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, New Year, Holi, Raksha Bandhan, Eid, Mother's Day, or Father's Day node exists anywhere in this nav tree - every one of those terms was grep-checked against the full rendered HTML and returned zero hits except 'Christmas' and (a false positive) 'holi' (matched inside 'holiday'/'Bank Holiday' shipping-policy text, not the festival). The 'Christmas' hits were individual product entries (e.g. 'Glass Christmas decoration', 'Christmas letter cushion', a 'Patterned fleece blanket' in a Christmas print) surfaced inside the generic New Arrivals / Textiles and Kids Room carousels; their embedded category codes resolve to ordinary categories (e.g. 'kids_kidsroom_products_decorations'), confirming these are seasonal-print SKUs living inside normal year-round categories, not a dedicated Christmas PLP - this is the 'category merely contains seasonal products' exclusion, not a genuine seasonal category. No 'Gifts' section exists in the nav at all. Tried guessing dedicated URLs (/en_in/home/christmas.html, /en_in/home/diwali.html, /en_in/home/festive.html, /en_in/home/shop-by-product/christmas-decorations.html) - christmas.html 30x-redirects to the plain homepage (soft-404 pattern, confirming no such page), the others were blocked or also non-resolving; none produced a distinct PLP. /en_in/sitemap.xml and /sitemap.xml both 404'd (no crawlable sitemap available). The site's internal search endpoint (/en_in/search-results.html?q=...) was consistently Akamai-blocked across both working iOS profiles and repeated attempts, so it could not be used as corroborating evidence, but per the task rules search absence is not required proof and was not relied upon - the conclusion rests on the fully enumerated, complete site-native mega-menu (the authoritative taxonomy) plus the confirmed soft-404 on every guessed holiday URL. Conclusion: H&M Home India carries a handful of Christmas-themed products (globally sourced SKUs with Christmas prints/names) merchandised inside its ordinary categories, but the India storefront presents no genuine seasonal/holiday PLP category for Christmas, Diwali, or any other festival - status is no_seasonal with rows: [].
